[![Help translate](https://img.shields.io/badge/Help-translate-6F42C1?logo=googletranslate&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor/pull/129)

Battery levels of your wireless mouse, headset, keyboard and controller, right on the Windows taskbar.

![Wireless Battery on the taskbar](docs/screenshot.png)

> **Just want it working?** Download **[WirelessBattery-Setup](https://github.com/krisgfx9/Wireless-Device-Battery-Monitor/releases/latest)** from the latest release, run it and click through. That's it.
>
> **Experienced users** can grab the portable zip, use the [command-line options](#command-line), or [build it from source](#build) with `make` or `build.bat`.
>
> **Like it?** Wireless Battery is free and open source. If it saves you a trip into vendor software, you can support it on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/krisgfx), [PayPal](https://www.paypal.com/paypalme/krisgfx) or [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/krisgfx9). It helps me keep my apps free alongside my studies. Not able to donate? A ⭐ star, sharing it, or reporting an unsupported device with a `--dump` helps just as much.

- **Tiny**: a ~350 KB app using about 2 MB of RAM. It's plain C++/Win32, with no runtime and no background service, and installs in seconds without admin rights.
- **No vendor software needed**: it talks to the devices directly. G HUB, Synapse, iCUE, GG and NGenuity can stay closed (or keep running; they don't conflict).
- **Many brands**: Logitech, Razer, SteelSeries, Corsair, HyperX, Glorious, Jabra, JBL, PlayStation and Xbox controllers, Samsung Galaxy Buds, any Bluetooth device Windows knows a battery level for, and every headset the bundled [HeadsetControl](https://github.com/Sapd/HeadsetControl) supports.

## Display

**On the taskbar (default):** `🎧 30%  🖱 93%` next to the notification area, drawn with the Windows icon font.
- **Low battery:** a red number means 15% or less.
- **Charging:** a blue ⚡ appears next to the number.
- **Asleep:** dimmed text means the device is asleep and the last known value is shown.
- **Two devices of one kind:** with two mice (or two controllers...) both would get the same icon, so each one gets a tiny caption of up to 3 letters in the corner of its icon, taken from its name (`MX`, `PRO`), or a number when the names do not tell them apart. A device that is alone in its kind shows no caption.
- **Theme:** it follows light/dark mode and DPI scaling.
- **Transparent taskbar themes** (e.g. Windhawk's Taskbar Styler): turn on *Background behind taskbar text* in the menu to keep the text readable over the wallpaper.
- **Several monitors:** the widget shows on every monitor's taskbar, next to its clock, so it stays visible while a game runs fullscreen. *Show the widget on* in the menu picks *All monitors*, *Main monitor only*, or one display (e.g. only *Display 3*).
- **More display options:** *Icons above percentages* stacks each icon over its level to save width; *Brand colors* shows known brands in their color (Razer green, HyperX red, ...) with a small level bar; two devices of the same kind get a tiny caption so they can be told apart; left and right taskbars get a column of devices.
- **Languages:** English, العربية, Deutsch, Español, Français, עברית, 日本語, Polski, Português (Brasil), Русский, Türkçe, 简体中文 and 繁體中文. The app follows the Windows display language; *Language* in the menu picks another one. See [Translations](#translations) to add or improve a language.
- **Brand colors:** devices of 15 known brands get their maker's color, with a soft glow and a thin level bar under the
  percentage: Razer green, Logitech blue, SteelSeries orange, Corsair yellow, HyperX / ROG / ZOWIE red, PlayStation,
  Xbox, Samsung, Apple, Jabra, JBL, Cooler Master and Steam. Each color has a dark- and a light-taskbar shade. The brand
  comes from the driver that found the device, then the vendor ID, then the name; colors and rules are in
  `src/brands.cpp`. Turn it off with *Brand colors* in the menu.

**Tray icons:** one icon per device with the number drawn in it, plus a "Low battery" notification at 15%. The app switches to this automatically when the taskbar is vertical or can't be found.

Hover for details. Click for the menu: every device (click one to hide or show it), display mode, *Refresh now*, *Start with Windows*, and *Exit*. Levels refresh every 60 seconds, and right away when a device is plugged in or the PC wakes up.

oss.readme:
Craft Anything

  English · 日本語 · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 한국어 · Español · Français · Tiếng Việt · Português · ไทย · Türkçe

  See how any website, app or game works, then have AI build your own version; an open-source, clean-room engine in pure Rust.
  Point it at a target, say what you want, and it studies the original with real inspection tools,
  has a coding agent build a new project, checks the result against the original and refines it.

  
  
  
  
  
  
  

  

  Download Craft Anything ·
  ArtCraft ·
  All Crafting Apps

  
  
  A website project: each check says how alike the build is, you approve anything outside the rules, and the plan shows what's left.

> [!NOTE]
> **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Painters, photographers,
> filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil
> last week. If you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

  How it works ·
  Two ways to use it ·
  AI ·
  Agents ·
  Under the hood ·
  Get started ·
  Status ·
  Downloads ·
  Discord

  
    
      🔍 Study anything
      Websites, desktop apps, phone apps, games and files: real inspection tools find out how they're built and what they do, with the evidence behind every answer.
    
    
      🛠️ Build your own
      Say what you want ("Recreate this website", "Recreate this game's gameplay in Rust") and a coding agent builds a new project in the stack you ask for.
    
    
      ✅ Checked, not guessed
      Every build is compared with the original (pages at three screen widths, a game's own self-test, an app's runs) and refined until it's close.
    
    
      🤖 Agent-ready
      320 tools, each one a CLI command and an MCP tool, so any agent can drive the same engine the app uses. No AI is needed to inspect.
    
  

## How it works

Point Craft Anything at a target, say what you want, and press Start. It works in four steps,
asking you in plain words when a decision is yours:

1. **Study:** inspect the original: its pages at every width, its code, its files, how it runs.
2. **Build:** a coding agent builds a new project, in the language, framework or engine your
   request names (or a sensible default).
3. **Check:** compare the build with the original and list what doesn't match yet.
4. **Ready:** open, play or preview the result, or ask for changes and it refines it.

  
    
      
      Make: pick what to recreate, say what you want, press Start.
    
    
      
      Ready: play the game, or ask for changes below.
    
  

## Two ways to use it

- **Simple** (default): "What do you want to make?" Pick a website, app or game, describe it,
  press Start. A project page shows the four steps (Study → Build → Check → Ready), what the
  agent is doing in plain words, question and approval cards, how alike the result is, and
  buttons to open the result or its folder. Ask for changes in the box at the bottom.
  "Just look inside" opens a target for questions without building anything (in Deep mode).
- **Advanced**: the full workbench: every tool (Ctrl/Cmd+K), functions, strings, pseudo-C,
  disassembly, hex, call graphs, evidence, unknowns, jobs, logs and the agent console.

Both modes drive the same engine.

## Clean room or Deep

- **Clean room** (the default): nothing inside the original is read, not its code, files or page
  source. Craft Anything works from what you can see: pictures you add, the website as a visitor
  sees it (screenshots, visible text, measured layout, colours, fonts and spacing, menus opened)
  and, when you allow it, a picture of the app's window. Tools that would look inside are refused
  and say how to turn on Deep mode.
- **Deep**: every tool is used, for your private use. A program's code and files are read with the
  built-in engines (and Ghidra when it's installed), a website's JavaScript is read and its start
  page watched, and the builder may use all of them.

Clean room is a rule about what Craft Anything offers and refuses. It is not an operating-system
sandbox: it doesn't isolate your computer. A coding agent you run still acts as you, and what it can
read, write or run depends on its own permissions. Which of an agent's own tools Craft Anything can
refuse differs by agent; for Claude Code's tools in chats and questions, see
[`docs/claude-code.md`](docs/claude-code.md).

Switch in the title bar or Settings, with `settings_set deep_mode true`, or for one CLI run with
`--deep` (or `--clean-room`).

  
  
  Advanced: functions, pseudo-C, the agent and the evidence behind every answer.

## AI

Building needs a coding agent on your computer. **Claude Code** is supported first: Craft
Anything runs your own, unmodified `claude` program, which uses your own sign-in; Craft Anything
never sees or handles your account. Your use of it falls under your own agreement with
Anthropic. See [docs/claude-code.md](docs/claude-code.md) for how and why. A Codex adapter
exists but hasn't been verified on a real install yet. **GitHub Copilot** can use your installed
Copilot CLI through ACP: sign in separately with `copilot login`. **Grok Build** can use your
installed `grok` program through ACP (`grok agent stdio`): sign in separately with `grok login`.
See [docs/grok.md](docs/grok.md). Other agents that speak ACP (Gemini CLI,
Qwen Code, opencode, goose, Hermes, Maki, Devin) can be switched to it per backend; of those, Maki
and Devin have been run live (Devin authenticates with the backend's stored key — its own CLI
sign-in doesn't count over ACP). Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, xAI (Grok, when `XAI_API_KEY` is
set) and local OpenAI-compatible servers are available for questions and analysis (Settings → AI).

oss.description: dsh-go — DeepSeek Harness 装进口袋：手机本机运行，也能遥控你的电脑。
oss.readme:
简体中文 · English

  
    
    
  

  DeepSeek Harness 的手机应用：Android 版已发布；iOS 版仍在开发和真机测试，需在 Mac 上自行签名编译（iOS 工程 · 架构）。

  
  
  
  

  
  Trendshift 全语言日榜 #1 · 2026-10-30

Deepy 和鲸娘，陪你干活

干活时敲代码，做完来个空翻，等你确认会举手。打开「App 外显示」，它们还会跟你到桌面。

     

     

下载 DSH Go

从 GitHub Releases 或官网下载页获取最新版 APK，常见手机选 arm64 包。

   

  感谢大家对 DSH Go 的支持和喜爱！当前下载页提供 Android APK；iOS 版还在开发和真机测试，没有公开安装包，鸿蒙版也在继续推进。

  

  第一次用可以先看使用指南，遇到问题欢迎来论坛和 QQ 群。
  手机上装过签名不同的早期测试包时不能直接覆盖安装，需要先卸载旧版；卸载会清空对话、Linux 环境和设置。

本机运行，也能遥控电脑

内置 Linux 环境，免 Root、免 Termux。电脑上的 DSH，也能一键切过去接着用。

  
    
    
  

插话、打断，过程自动收好

回复中途也能插话，排队的消息随时「立即发送」。做完的过程折叠成一行。

  
    
    
  

原生界面，也有网页版

和官方网页版一键切换，停在同一段对话，下次打开还是你上次用的那个。

  
    
    
  

分享卡、对话回放和链接

回复一键做成分享卡。整段对话生成链接，对方在浏览器里回放，链接端到端加密。

  
    
    
  

横屏与平板

横屏手机和平板重新排版：侧栏常驻，内容居中，弹出键盘也不挤。

  
    
    
  

主题配色与桌面图标

六套主题色，也能跟随壁纸或自选颜色。四款桌面图标，三种功能图标风格。

  
    
    
  

中文，也说 English

全部界面支持英文，在设置里切换，默认跟随系统。

  
    
    
  

手机操控

看屏幕、帮你点，三档确认随你选。敏感操作默认交还给你；放宽应用规则或解除限制前，请先了解风险。

  
    
    
  

## 可以做什么

DSH Go 提供聊天界面、本机运行环境和远程连接，是基于 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的第三方项目。运行在手机上的是 DSH 引擎；模型请求仍由你配置的模型提供方处理。

- **本机运行**：在 App 内安装 Ubuntu、Node.js 与 DSH 运行环境，无需 Root 或另装 Termux。
- **远程连接**：通过 SSH 或李国宝老师开发的 [DSHarness Remote](https://github.com/liguobao/ds-harness-remote) 使用电脑、服务器上的 DSH。
- **聊天与工具**：切换模型，发送图片、使用语音输入，处理工具审批和提问；支持聊天界面与网页模式。
- **插件界面**：使用适配 DSH Go 的原生工具卡、表单和面板；仓库提供 SDK、教程和示例。
- **手机操控**：在你开启权限后，让本机引擎读取屏幕、点按和输入，并可随时停止。
- **分享与外观**：分享、导出和回放对话，调整主题、图标和桌宠。

功能随主机和连接方式不同。DSHarness Remote 当前只支持图片附件，不能在 App 内打开网页版，插件管理限于开关，且不支持 DS Bot 和对话日志导出。详见[本机引擎与远程主机](docs/guide/zh/03-engine-hosts.md)。

## 安装

安装要求为 Android 8.0（API 26）及以上。Release 页面上的 **arm64** 安装包适用于常见的 64 位 Android 手机；x86_64 设备和模拟器用的 x64 包在发布说明末尾的「其他版本下载」里。仓库没有 32 位 ARM 构建。

1. 从 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go/releases/latest) 或[官网下载页](https://go.dshtui.com/download)下载对应架构的 APK，并按系统提示允许该安装来源。
2. 首次启动时，选择在本机安装运行环境，或连接远程主机。
3. 为所选主机配置模型和所需凭据，再开始对话；部分远程渠道需要在主机侧配置。

仅连接远程主机时，不必在手机上安装本机运行环境。手机操控只对正常模式下的本机引擎开放，需要按界面说明开启无障碍等权限；不打扰模式另外要求 Android 14 及以上，以及 Shizuku 或自连 ADB。首次使用可按[使用指南](docs/guide/README.md)逐项配置。

本地引擎默认使用 PRoot 兼容启动。开发者选项中的直接启动默认关闭，开启后的兼容性和回退方式见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。当前 Android 构建以 APK 侧载为目标，不是 Google Play 发布配置。

## 数据与权限

模型请求会发送给你配置的提供方。开启手机操控后，任务需要的屏幕文字可能发送给模型，支持看图的模型也可能收到截图；请先阅读 App 的权限说明。

“发送匿名使用统计”默认开启，可在首次引导或“设置 → 隐私与分享”关闭。采集范围和关闭后的处理见[常见问题](docs/guide/zh/11-faq.md)。分享内容前，请检查预览；收到链接或文件的人可以保存其中的内容。

## 常见问题

和 DeepSeek 官方是什么关系？

没有关系。DSH Go 是社区开发的非官方客户端，基于开源的 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 构建。手机上运行的是 DSH 本身；模型请求发给你配置的模型提供方，需要联网，按你在提供方的账户计费。

安全吗？

本机网页版只接受 App 自己的访问。分享链接端到端加密，密钥只在链接里，服务器看不到内容，但获得完整链接的人可以读取并保存内容。手机操控默认保留敏感操作保护；放宽应用规则或开启「解除限制」会减少这些保护。安全机制不能保证零风险，详见[风险提示与免责声明](#风险提示与免责声明)和[手机操控指南](docs/guide/zh/04-phone-control.md)。

切到后台会被杀吗？

部分系统的省电策略会拦住后台。DSH Go 发现后会提醒你，并直达对应的放行设置，vivo、小米、华为、荣耀、OPPO 都有。

## 从源码构建

以下流程面向 **Linux x86_64**。当前工具链脚本默认安装 JDK 17、Flutter 3.47.7 和 Android SDK/NDK；App 要求 Dart `^3.13.5`。准备 Bash、Git、curl、tar、unzip、xz、Python 3、zstd（Python 未提供 `compression.zstd` 时用于解包 zstd 压缩的 deb）、file 和常见 GNU 命令；重新解析 Ubuntu 软件包锁时还需要 gpgv。

先取得完整源码和项目资源。`app/pubspec.yaml` 声明的字体、图片等都是构建输入，运行时包由下面的脚本生成。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-go.git
cd dsh-go

bash tooling/setup-toolchain.sh
source tooling/env.sh
flutter --version
java -version

bash runtime/build-runtime.sh arm64-v8a
DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh -f arm64 --keep-daemon
```

工具链脚本会下载 SDK/NDK 与模拟器镜像，并执行 Android SDK 许可接受步骤。默认安装到 `~/dev`；可通过 `DEV_ROOT` 指定独立目录。脚本会复用已有安装，构建前请核对版本。

产物为 `app/build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-arm64-release.apk`。运行时构建使用仓库固定的版本与校验信息，并需要联网下载依赖。示例中的 `DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE=` 不嵌入维护者的内测通道令牌；`--keep-daemon` 保留 Gradle daemon，适合同时开发其他 Android 项目的环境。

构建 x86_64 包时，先生成对应运行时：

```bash
bash runtime/build-runtime.sh x86_64
DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh -f x64 --keep-daemon
```

未配置 `app/android/key.properties` 时，本地 release 构建使用 debug 签名。它不能直接覆盖不同签名的官方安装包；请在测试设备上安装，保留已有数据，不要为解决签名冲突直接卸载正在使用的 App。发布签名与密钥文件不要提交到仓库。

只查看 APK 构建命令，可运行：

```bash
DSH_BETA_TOKEN_FILE= bash tooling/build-apk.sh --dry-run -f all
```

oss.description: Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time, checked against the original's recorded behavior at every step. CLIs, HTTP servers and libraries in TypeScript, Python, C, Go, Ruby and Java.
oss.readme:
rust-anything

by erKam Yaman

English · Türkçe · Українська · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · Deutsch · Français · Русский · 日本語 · 한국어 · Azərbaycanca · Oʻzbekcha · Қазақша · Кыргызча · Türkmençe · Татарча · ئۇيغۇرچە · Português

Rewrite your whole app in Rust. Keep it working the whole way.

CLIs, servers and libraries, piece by piece, checked against the original at every step.

Node.js and TypeScript · Python · C · Go · Ruby · Java · PHP and C# in preview

  
  
  
  
  
  
  

  Quick start ·
  Languages ·
  How it works ·
  The loop ·
  Port a whole app ·
  Hot paths ·
  Install ·
  What it can't catch ·
  FAQ

up to 20x faster · 38,251 recorded cases replayed · 0 mismatches · one command

  
  
  Typing a query into x18n's search over 50,000 keys: the TypeScript original against the rust-anything batch, same results at every keystroke.

  
    
      Record
      record runs the original on generated edge cases, semantic traps and your own inputs, and saves what it returns or throws.
    
    
      Port
      bridge generates the Rust crate and a wrapper, so callers keep the original API. You or your agent write the Rust.
    
    
      Check
      diff replays every recorded case against the Rust, and nothing ships until they all match and gate passes.
    
    
      Lift
      When replay passes with no fallback and every unit passes gate, app lift makes it a pure Rust app. The original is never touched.
    
  

**Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time.** rust-anything records what your
Node.js (TypeScript/JavaScript), Python, C, Go, Ruby or Java app does today, then checks every piece of the
Rust rewrite against that recording before it moves on, until the app is pure Rust. CLIs, HTTP
servers and libraries; your coding agent (or you) writes the Rust. It can only catch what the
recording covers: see [What it can't catch](docs/how-it-works.md#what-it-cant-catch). Only need the slow part fast?
Port just that, one hot path at a time:

| Real workload, same results as the original | Original | With rust-anything |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| x18n's sidebar search, 50,000 keys (TypeScript, Node) | 10 ms per query | **0.5 ms: 20x faster** |
| The same search in the browser (wasm, one thread) | 10 ms | **0.95 ms: 11.5x** |
| `slugify` over 20,000 strings (Python) | 98 ms | **17x faster** |
| `Shellwords.shellescape` from Ruby's standard library, 50,000 values | 88 ms | **11.8x faster** |
| `Slugify` over 50,000 strings (Go) | 49 ms | **4x faster** |
| `slugify` over 50,000 strings (Java) | 43 ms | **3x faster** |

Measured on 4 cores; every number has a benchmark in [`demo/`](./demo) that first checks the
results are identical. Calling Rust once per small function is usually *slower* than a JIT;
rust-anything finds the loop worth moving, and moves it.

> rust-anything is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by the Rust Project
> or the Rust Foundation. "Rust" is a trademark of the Rust Foundation.

> [!WARNING]
> `record` and `app record` run your original code, calling each function (or the whole app) on
> many generated inputs, and `app record` runs every case twice. `diff`, `gate` and `app replay`
> run the same cases again, on the port or the original. Code that writes files, talks to a
> database or calls the network does that once per case. Run them on a copy of the project, with a
> test database and no production credentials in the environment.

## Quick start

Paste this into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini CLI and let your agent install it:

```text
Install rust-anything: run `cargo install rust-anything`, then `rust-anything setup`.
Tell me when to restart you.
```

Or yourself:

```sh
cargo install rust-anything   # from crates.io
rust-anything setup           # registers it with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI
```

No Rust toolchain yet? Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows are attached to each
[GitHub release](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/releases), and for JavaScript
projects `npm install -g rust-anything` installs the same binary.

In Claude Code you can also install it as a plugin (the MCP server and the skill; the CLI above
must be on your `PATH`):

```text
/plugin install rust-anything --marketplace erkamyaman/rust-anything
```

`setup` adds the MCP server to each agent it finds and installs the workflow skill where the agent
reads skills. It keeps your other settings, is safe to run again, and `--remove` undoes it.
Then ask your agent, for example:

- *"Rewrite this CLI in Rust with rust-anything, end to end, and prove it behaves the same."*
- *"This search feels slow. Profile it with rust-anything and move the hot loop to Rust."*
- *"Plan a migration of `src/parser/` to Rust with rust-anything; port the first unit and prove it."*
- *"Bench the Rust port in `rust/text-rs` against the original and tell me whether to ship it."*

### Works with

| Agent | `rust-anything setup` adds |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | MCP server in `~/.claude.json`, skill in `~/.claude/skills/` |
| Codex | MCP server in `~/.codex/config.toml`, skill in `~/.codex/skills/` |
| Cursor | MCP server in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` |
| Gemini CLI | MCP server in `~/.gemini/settings.json` |
| Any other MCP client | add `rust-anything mcp` as a stdio server by hand (see [Install](docs/install.md#install)) |

Before changing a file that exists, `setup` saves a copy beside it (`.rust-anything.bak`).

Or run the steps yourself:

  
  
  The steps on x18n's fuzzyScore: profile finds the hot loop, bridge --batch generates the crate, gate passes, and the benchmark compares it with the TypeScript.

```sh
rust-anything profile . -- node bench.mjs              # what is hot, and who calls it
rust-anything bridge . src/fuzzy.ts --batch fuzzyScore:text
# write src/port.rs (or let your agent), then:
rust-anything record rust/fuzzy-rs && rust-anything build rust/fuzzy-rs
rust-anything diff rust/fuzzy-rs                       # every recorded case must match
rust

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Why switch from IDM?

**Same window you know. Your downloads finish sooner. And it costs nothing.**

  
    
    
  

| | Mister Download Manager | IDM 6.42 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Download a big file (1 GB) | **1 second** | 5.5 seconds |
| Download a small file | **instantly** | 3.1 seconds |
| Download over a shaky connection | **1.6 seconds** | 5.4 seconds |
| Wait before a download starts | **instantly** | 3.1 seconds |
| Price | **Free, forever** | Paid, after a 30-day trial |
| Ads, nag screens, sign-up | **None** | Registration needed |
| Open source | **Yes** (GPL) | No |

Nothing new to learn: the toolbar, the categories, the list of downloads, the progress window and
the browser button are where you expect them. Measured on the same computer, downloading from a
test server on that computer (a loopback test: it times the programs, not an internet connection),
same files, both programs at their default settings ([how we measured](#the-benchmark-in-detail)).

## Download

  
  
  

On the [download page](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/releases/latest), pick
one:

| File | Choose it when |
| --- | --- |
| **`...-setup.exe`** | **Not sure? Take this one.** It installs MDM, connects it to your browser and asks your language. |
| `...-portable.zip` | You want MDM on a USB stick or without installing: unzip and run. Everything stays in its folder. |
| `...-x64.zip` | You want the plain programs without an installer. |
| `...-setup-arm64.exe`, `...-portable-arm64.zip`, `...-arm64.zip` | The same three for **Windows on ARM** (Snapdragon and other ARM PCs). |
| `...-setup-x86.exe`, `...-portable-x86.zip`, `...-x86.zip` | The same three for **32-bit Windows 10**. There, choose your own ffmpeg in **Helpers** for the best video qualities: none is built for it that MDM can check. |
| `...-extension-chromium.zip` | You want to add the browser extension by hand (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi). From the stores is easier: [Add to Chrome](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/mister-download-manager/ejoleppdfgjdndddcjoehopknmlglojp), [Add to Firefox](https://addons.mozilla.org/firefox/addon/mister-download-manager/). |

The ARM64 and 32-bit files come with every release after 0.5.2; **Check for updates** keeps each
copy on its own processor's files.

> [!NOTE]
> Windows may say *"Windows protected your PC"* the first time, because this early version isn't
> code-signed yet. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

Or with [WinGet](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/package-manager/winget/), Windows' package
manager: in a terminal, the first line installs MDM and the second updates it.

```
winget install AhmedNefzaoui.MisterDownloadManager
winget upgrade AhmedNefzaoui.MisterDownloadManager
```

### Code signing policy

Free code signing provided by [SignPath.io](https://about.signpath.io), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org).
Which Windows files are signed, who reviews and approves them, and what MDM sends over the
network: [code signing policy](https://misterdownloadmanager.com/code-signing-policy.html).

### On Linux

MDM runs on Linux too, tested on Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 12 and Fedora with GNOME, KDE Plasma, Xfce
and Cinnamon, on X11 and in Wayland sessions: the tray, dark mode, browser integration (Ubuntu's
Snap Firefox included) and the packages' installs. Not there yet: screen readers (Orca) don't
read its windows, and Flatpak browsers can't reach it ([more](docs/getting-started.md#on-linux)).
Up to version 0.2.4, the files' names end in `-experimental`.

| File | For |
| --- | --- |
| `...-linux-x86_64.deb` | Ubuntu, Debian, Mint, Pop!_OS: `sudo apt install ./.deb`. |
| `...-linux-x86_64.rpm` | Fedora, openSUSE, RHEL: `sudo dnf install ./.rpm`. |
| `...-linux-x86_64.AppImage` | Any Linux. Make it executable and run it. |
| `...-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | The plain programs, for any distribution. |
| `...-linux-arm64.*` | The same four for 64-bit ARM computers, from the release after 0.5.2 (built and tested on GitHub's ARM machines). |

  
    
    
  

### On a Mac? Be the first to try it

Fresh builds for **macOS** (Apple Silicon and Intel) are on the same download page, marked
`-experimental`: we haven't tried them on a Mac ourselves yet. Give them a go and
[tell us how it went](https://github.com/anefzaoui/misterdownloadmanager/issues/new/choose); you'll
help make them as solid as the Windows and Linux versions.

| File | For |
| --- | --- |
| `...-macos-arm64-experimental.dmg` | Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or later). Open it and drag MDM to Applications. The first time, right-click the app and choose **Open**. |
| `...-macos-x86_64-experimental.dmg` | Mac with an Intel processor, the same way. |

## 🌍 In your language

Every language Windows 11 offers, **86 in all**. MDM asks on its first start, and you can change
it any time in **View → Language**.

GestaltX

[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.6-blue)](https://github.com/huamidev/GestaltX)
[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/iOS-27.x-black?logo=apple)](#compatibility)

[English](README.md) · [简体中文](README_ZH-CN.md) · [日本語](README_JA.md) · [한국어](README_KO.md) · [Türkçe](README_TR.md)

A MobileGestalt editor for iPhone and iPad. Developed by [huamidev](https://github.com/huamidev).

## Features

| Category | Presets and tools |
| --- | --- |
| Display | Dynamic Island capability and layout, Always-On Display, AOD Vibrancy, high-luminance AOD, AOD flipbook, HDR photo display, wallpaper parallax, Liquid Glass low-power rendering, experimental PWM and DisplayPort flags |
| Device | Model name, boot/shutdown chime, charge limit, tap to wake, Camera Control settings, Action Button settings, Collision SOS, Audio Mix, Spatial FaceTime audio |
| iPad | Apple Pencil settings, Stage Manager capability, iPad app compatibility |
| Intelligence | Independent region-code options, Apple Intelligence capability flag, on-device Siri, Audio Intelligence, Personal Translator, Photos Clean Up, Handwriting Synthesis, always-listening Hey Siri, and sales-region options for activation attempts on China-mainland devices |
| Advanced | Apple internal feature flags, the system-wide InternalBuild flag with explicit enable confirmation, internal settings bundle, Security Research Device flag |
| Field editor | Read, search, add, edit, and remove `CacheExtra` fields; local plist import/export; String, Integer, Real, Boolean, Data, Date, Array, and Dictionary values |
| Changes | Automatic reading and manual re-read, staged before/after review, verified writes, per-preset restore |
| Backups | Automatic initial backup before device editing, backup before every write, original-value records; open, export, restore, and delete |
| Logs & respring | Actual exploit-stage logs and manual NeoSpring respring |

Usually, changing the region code is enough to try enabling AI; there is no need to change Sales Region. Selecting United States for Region Code sets `RegionCode` to `LL` and keeps the sales-region suffix. You can also choose China (Mainland), Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan or the United Kingdom. Sales Region and Region Code can be applied together: the sales suffix follows Sales Region, while the code follows Region Code.

*If you previously changed Sales Region, restore your device’s original sales region and apply it first.*

Disabling a preset or using its Revert button restores the recorded original values and types. Keys that were originally absent are removed. If an older change has no original record, use Remove Added Fields only when you know those fields were added.

Presets modify capability flags; actual effects depend on the device and OS. China-mainland devices can use the Apple Intelligence and region options to attempt activation; availability also depends on the model, OS version, and Apple services.

### Apple Intelligence, Face ID and dictation

The [YumEdit 1.2.1 approach](https://github.com/H4CNPE/YumEdit/tree/v1.2.1) avoids spoofing the product, board and CPU. In Intelligence, **Apple Intelligence Capability** sets the generative-model flag to `1`, while the separate **Siri AI Mode** preset sets `SiriMode` to `2`. Neither changes hardware identity nor the device-specific On-Device Siri capability. These are experimental flags, not a guarantee of resource downloads or working Apple Intelligence. YumEdit later replaced this activation approach with an experimental two-stage workflow; GestaltX does not implement temporary hardware spoofing.

If a previous hardware spoof broke Face ID or dictation, choose an original device backup in **Backups → Restore Hardware Identity**. Alternatively, import a verified original plist and use **Intelligence → Restore Hardware Identity**. Save or discard pending changes first. Recovery requires a verified same-device backup with the same `CacheData`, `CacheUUID` and cache version, whose product and board match the kernel-reported hardware. It restores only product, board, CPU and the original regulatory model number, preserving current AI, Siri, region and unrelated settings. Unlike YumEdit's region activation, recovery does not substitute a US regulatory model. Missing, incompatible or already-spoofed backups are rejected; original hardware values are never guessed.

Recovery currently recognizes iPhone 11 through iPhone 15/15 Plus (including the second- and third-generation SE), checking the original CPU against the known chip for the physical product. Other products are rejected rather than guessing their chip. A backup is created before writing and the complete result is verified. **Fully restart the device, then test Face ID, dictation and Apple Intelligence.** This recovery addresses hardware-spoofing damage, not every possible Face ID fault; device-level behavior still requires testing on affected hardware.

## Compatibility

Supports **iOS / iPadOS 27.x**. **iOS / iPadOS 26.x is not supported for on-device MobileGestalt access.** Powered by [worse_query](https://github.com/forcequitOS/worse_query). SystemGroup access requires iOS 27; available features depend on the device and OS. Local plist editing is also supported.

Signing requires a certificate and provisioning profile with at least one usable App Group. Sign the app and its embedded share extension with at least one **common App Group**, and keep the extension when re-signing. Both processes detect their actual signed App Groups at runtime. Distributed IPAs carry ad-hoc signatures with these entitlements embedded so SideStore and AltStore can detect them when re-signing; they are not signed with a developer certificate.

releases.name: sdk-v1.10.0
releases.body:
### Features

* **api:** add beta support for the billing_policy request parameter
* **api:** add contract_spend_limit_reached error code to messages
* **api:** add error codes for linked billing refusals
* **api:** add the user_profile_billing_not_authorized error code
* **api:** add webhook events for external key failure and recovery


### Bug Fixes

* **tools:** keep the session tool runner's maxIdleMs countdown running when a session thread terminates

  If the runner fails to read the session's event history after a reconnect, a termination that then arrives on the event stream still cancels the countdown, until the next idle or successful read.

* **tools:** stop EnvironmentWorker from running tools for a terminated session

  For a terminated session, the worker now force-stops the work item right after it retrieves the session, before it downloads skills or memory stores. It no longer throws `SessionMemoryError` for such a session. The API reports an archived session as `terminated`.

* **tools:** stop the session tool runner from running the tool calls of a terminated session thread

  The runner also stops waiting for a confirmation of these calls and no longer yields them, including a denied call (`confirmation: 'deny'`) and a call to a tool that it does not own. A call that the runner starts before it reads the session thread's `session.thread_status_terminated` event still runs to the end, and the runner yields it with `posted: false` when the API refuses the result.


### Chores

* **api:** rename error data models, deprecating the old names
* **docs:** clarify which AWS KMS keys a workspace can use on Claude Platform on AWS
* **docs:** clarify which credential work get, update and list accept
* **docs:** clarify which uploads a plugin pin holds back
* **docs:** note that a plugin scan's reason also covers errored scans

  `content_scan.reason` on an errored scan now says why there is no verdict. It is not a security finding, so code that treats any `reason` as a concern should also check `status`.
